# Terraform

<http://registry.terraform.io/providers/hashicorp/aws/latest/docs>

**Terraform is an infrastructure as code (IaC) tool that lets you build, change, and manage cloud and on-premises resources using human-readable configuration files**.

**HCL** : HashiCorp Configuration Language

**AWS**: CloudFormation templates

create a file with .tf extension in a directory and run the following commands:

**terraform init** : This is use to initialize the terraform in the working directory

**terraform plan** : This is a kind of dry run command which helps us to tell which is going to be happen

**terraform apply** : This is a actual command which run the script and apply the changes on the provider

**terraform destroy** : This command is use to destroy the created items by terraform as per the script

**terraform validate**: This command actually validate the script

**terraform console**: This command is use to start interactive terminal

**terraform refresh**: This command is use to sync the state file with the configuration of the cloud services. Means if you had done some manual changes in the AWS like adding description from the aws dashboard, this command will sync the changes to the state file

**terraform fmt**: This command is use to format the script like correcting the indentation and spacing

**terraform taint**: This coommand is use to mark a resource as tainted (means that this resource is been damaged). You can manually mark a specific resource as tained by below command or terraform also mark a resource as tainted in a condition where it found error in creation of resource

`terraform taint aws_security_group.allow_tls`

terraform graph: This command is use to generate graph of the current script or setup. Here is an example command to create graph in pdf

`terraform graph | dot -Tpdf > graph.pdf`

**--var-file dev-terraform.tfvars**: This is a flag which you can use to mention the specific file name instead of going with the traditional naming convension of the files. You can use this flag with "plan" or "apply"

**terraform workspace**: This is use to manage the multiple workspaces in a single project. It basically create multiple state files for each workspace to maintain the state. Initially, There is always a "default" workspace.

`terraform workspace list`

This is use to list all workspaces

`terraform workspace new dev`

This command is use to create a new workspace with the name of "Dev"

`terraform workspace show`

This show the name of current workspace

`terraform workspace select prod`

This command is use to switch workspace

---

## Parts of Terraform

**Provider**: This can be aws, azure, gcp. This basically means that what is the cloud platform where we want to create resource

**Resource**: This is configuration of the resource which needs to be creates. For example, here we declared like ec2 or s3 for aws provider

**Variables**:

1. **input variables**: This is an actually which value which we share as variable and reuse it anywhere in the template script
2. **output variables**: This is just to print output when the script runs

**provisioner:** These are special kind of instruction written in terraform script which helps us in executing custom commands like copying file from local to remote directory or running installation command in the remote ec2 instance

<https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/provisioners>

- [ ] file: This provisioner is use to execute/read file content in remote
- [ ] local-exec: This provisioner is use to run the command or code on the local machine ( in current directory as default )
- [ ] remote-exec: This provisioner is use to run the command or code on the remote machine.

**terraform.tfvars** file: This is a default file name which is use to manage and overwrite the variable values at runtime while creation of resources

**modules**: This is a way to modularize the structure of terraform into modules and multiple files which we can reuse on the basis of required inputs

**terraform**: This section is use to define configuration or validation of the terraform. For example, if you want to have a consistent terraform version for all the developer who are updating/working on this project then you can mention it in here. Also, in this section is it restricted to use variables.

There is a section "backend" which is use to host state file remotly in case of multiple developers involvement.

Note:&#x20;

1. use "self" keyword in case if we need to reference a resource inside a same block. Below is the example to it
2. use "when" keyword in case when you need to run script/code during a specific event like destroy of resource
3. use "on\_failure=continue" is use to handle in case of error/failure
4. Always remember that  terraform do not track the changes in script files. meaning if you make any change in the script without changing the terraform file, the terraform do not able to track

you can names it anything but in those cases you need to provide file name to the 'apply' command like this:

```ts
terraform apply dev.tfvars
```

How to loop?

Below code is responsible for executing the loop but this code need to be in some resource block

```tsx
dynamic "ingress" "allow_tls" {
for_each = [1,2,3,4,5,6]
iterator = port
content {
to = port.value
}
}
```
